scope: Exploratory activation analysis on synthetic language prompts; not a complete interpretation or biological validation.

method.layer_selection: Validation ROC AUC, then validation effect size
method.null_layer_selection: Each null iteration independently selects its best validation layer before test evaluation

selected_attention_head.selection: Validation ROC AUC after training-set direction construction

interpretation: The validation-selected residual direction achieved stress-test ROC AUC 0.6875, above every one of 200 shuffled-label and 200 random-direction null runs after each null repeated layer selection. Residual intervention shifted the Yes-minus-No margin positively on 11 of 12 negative prompts. Finer localization was weak: the validation-selected attention head fell to ROC AUC 0.583 on stress testing, individual training-ranked MLP neurons reached at most 0.649, and replacing the eight selected MLP activations with negative-training means did not reduce the output margin on most positive prompts. The evidence supports a distributed residual-stream association and intervention sensitivity in this authored dataset, not a stable semantic feature, localized mechanism, or complete causal circuit.
limitations: All prompt sets were authored for this experiment; the larger test set is fixed and versioned but not externally independent or formally preregistered.
The stress test broadens formats and vocabulary but does not eliminate dataset-construction confounds.
Empirical p-values are finite-control diagnostics for this prompt set, not population-level significance claims.
Head localization uses pre-output-projection channel blocks and does not isolate query, key, value, or attention-pattern mechanisms.
MLP localization evaluates eight training-ranked intermediate neurons and does not resolve interactions or multiple-comparison uncertainty.
Activation replacement with a negative-training mean is one intervention baseline and may create off-distribution internal states.
Intervention sensitivity is not semantic proof or biological validation.
Results on Gemma 3 270M do not establish behavior of Gemma 4 31B or another checkpoint.
The bfloat16 results are not claimed to be numerically identical across hardware, drivers, or library versions.
No GMP, process-control, product-quality, clinical, or patient-safety conclusion is supported.
